reference.source: DeVita, Hellman and Rosenberg's Cancer / NCCN genetic/familial guidelines
clinicalPearls: Caused by germline pathogenic variants in SMAD4 or BMPR1A, both components of the BMP/TGF-beta signalling pathway, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern
Characterised by multiple hamartomatous juvenile polyps throughout the gastrointestinal tract, most often colorectal but also gastric and small-bowel
The term juvenile refers to the histological polyp type, not the age of the patient, and polyps carry a raised risk of colorectal and gastric cancer
SMAD4 carriers may have a combined phenotype with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia, so screening for arteriovenous malformations is important
Presentation is often with gastrointestinal bleeding, anaemia, protein-losing enteropathy or intussusception in childhood or early adulthood
Surveillance relies on regular colonoscopy and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with polypectomy, and risk-reducing colectomy or gastrectomy is considered when polyp burden becomes unmanageable
Massive gastric polyposis is more typical of SMAD4-related disease and can require surgical management
reference.pathophysiology: The syndrome arises from germline loss-of-function variants in SMAD4 or BMPR1A, genes that transmit bone morphogenetic protein and transforming growth factor-beta signals regulating epithelial and stromal growth in the gut. Disruption of this pathway impairs the normal restraint on cell proliferation and alters the epithelial-mesenchymal interactions of the intestinal wall, favouring the development of hamartomatous polyps. Accumulation of further somatic changes within these polyps underlies the progression to dysplasia and gastrointestinal malignancy.
additionalDifferentials: PTEN hamartoma tumour syndrome (Cowden and related conditions)
additionalInvestigations: Germline SMAD4 and BMPR1A sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis
Colonoscopy with polypectomy and histological confirmation of juvenile-type polyps
Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy to assess gastric and duodenal polyps
Full blood count and iron studies to detect chronic blood loss and anaemia
Screening for hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia features in SMAD4 carriers, including pulmonary and cerebral vascular assessment
Cross-sectional or capsule imaging of the small bowel where indicated
redFlags: Significant or recurrent gastrointestinal bleeding with anaemia
Rapidly increasing polyp burden or a focal mass suggesting malignant change
Features of pulmonary or cerebral arteriovenous malformation in a SMAD4 carrier
Intussusception or obstruction from large polyps
reference.prognosis: With regular endoscopic surveillance and polypectomy most patients are managed effectively, but cumulative gastrointestinal cancer risk is substantial and increases with polyp burden. SMAD4 carriers require additional vigilance for vascular malformations, and severe gastric polyposis can necessitate surgery, so lifelong multidisciplinary follow-up is needed.
pitfalls: Confusing sporadic solitary juvenile polyps in children with the inherited syndrome
Overlooking the hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia overlap and its vascular complications in SMAD4 carriers
Focusing on the colon and neglecting gastric surveillance where cancer risk is also raised
Failing to offer cascade genetic testing to at-risk relatives
references: DeVita, Hellman and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology
NCCN Guidelines: Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment - Colorectal
management: Clear polyps by endoscopic polypectomy at colonoscopy and upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with histological confirmation of juvenile-type polyps
Maintain lifelong endoscopic surveillance of colon, stomach and small bowel, with frequency dictated by polyp number and dysplasia
Replace iron and manage anaemia, gastrointestinal bleeding and protein-losing enteropathy
Reserve risk-reducing colectomy or gastrectomy for unmanageable polyposis or high-grade dysplasia
Screen SMAD4 carriers for arteriovenous malformations of the lungs and brain given overlap with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia
Provide genetic counselling and germline SMAD4/BMPR1A testing with cascade screening of at-risk relatives
Manage within a multidisciplinary medical genetics, gastroenterology and surgical team
